name: Motion and fitness activity
plain: Reads step counts and whether the person is walking, running, driving or cycling.
meaning: Reveals daily routine, commute mode and exercise habits, and works as a coarse movement log even without location.

android.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't allow physical activity
android.persistence: Until revoked; auto-reset after months unused
android.store_policy: Play: sensitive health and activity data policy
android.api_surface: SensorManager TYPE_STEP_COUNTER, ActivityRecognitionClient (Play services), Health Services
android.note: Android 9 and lower needed no permission for step counter

ios.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't Allow motion and fitness
ios.note: Historical queries reach back about 7 days

limits.headline: Can see your steps and whether you walk, run, drive or cycle, after you allow
limits.user_action: You tap Allow for Motion and Fitness (iPhone) or Physical activity (Android)
can: Count your steps and walking distance
Tell whether you walk, run, drive or cycle
Look back about 7 days of history on iPhone
Use Health Connect or Play services on Android
cannot: Run the sensors if you turn the permission off
Use step counters on Android 10 and newer without the permission
limits.differs: Android 9 and older needed no permission for the step counter. iPhone keeps about 7 days of motion history.

story.what_it_is: An app reads your step counts and whether you are walking, running, driving or cycling.

marketing.name: Motion and Fitness
marketing.pitch: Apple's setting that lets apps show your steps, distance and activity from your iPhone's motion sensors.

marketing.name: Physical activity
marketing.pitch: Android lets apps know about your physical activity so they can count steps and detect workouts.

story.for_you: You see a prompt asking to access Motion and Fitness, or Physical activity on Android. If you agree, the app shows your steps and may start a workout when you begin to move. If you say no, those features turn off.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to track steps cheaply, power fitness rewards and detect drives. It also reveals your daily routine, like when you commute, work out and sleep, even without GPS.

use_cases.example: A step counter shows your steps and a goal ring that fills up as you walk.
A game gives coins for the distance you walk in the real world.
A health app notes how active you are and tells your doctor if you stop moving.
A car insurer's app detects that you are driving and scores braking and speed.
A rewards app pays points for steps, which keeps you coming back every day.
A watch app syncs steps and activity type with the phone.

story.android_note: Android calls this Physical activity, and it is a runtime permission on Android 10 and later.
story.ios_note: iPhone calls this Motion and Fitness and shows a prompt the first time an app asks.

technical_bounds: History window about 7 days on iOS
No raw accelerometer data is returned by these APIs
